success_patterns: Set-completion clues ('Brahma, Shiva & this one') were answered with the one missing member of the group. The agent skipped the names already in the clue and picked the remaining member that the passages list in every mention of the group.

'Type of this material' and 'traditional color of X' clues were answered with a single bare common noun ('rubber', 'red') that the passages repeatedly tie to the clue's anchor. The agent did not copy modifiers from the clue ('synthetic rubber') or add a descriptor.

Each clue was matched on its distinctive anchor words (neoprene, Trimurti, London double-decker). The agent answered with the entity that the context sentences about that anchor kept repeating, and its own knowledge agreed with them.

patch.reasoning: All three successes were short, well-supported answers to clues with a clear slot type. Two patterns are not stated explicitly in the skill: the missing-member-of-a-set clue, and the common-noun answer for 'type of this material / traditional color' clues. Earlier broad edits were rejected, so both additions are small, concrete and aimed at the slot type, to avoid disturbing the existing rules.

edits.target: - Clue lists its own options ('Of North Park, East Park, West Park or South Park, it's where...'): the answer is exactly one of the listed options, copied verbatim. Use the context to pick which.
edits.content: - Set-completion clues ('The Trimurti consists of Brahma, Shiva & this one', 'Athos, Porthos & this musketeer'): the names in the clue are given. The answer is the remaining member of the group, the one the passages list next to those names every time ('Vishnu'). Never repeat a name already in the clue.

edits.target: - Give only the MISSING part. If a word from the clue is part of the answer phrase, do not repeat it
edits.content: (e.g. 'neoprene is a synthetic type of this material' -> 'rubber', not 'synthetic rubber'; 'the traditional color of London's double-decker buses' -> 'red'). For 'type of this material / traditional color / this one' clues, give the single bare common noun or adjective the passages tie to the clue's anchor, with no modifiers copied from the clue
